html:
The Khanate of Bukhara was an Uzbek state in Central Asia, ruled from Bukhara by Chinggisid khans from 1500 to 1785. It is one of the Uzbek khanates. On this map in 1530 the label is drawn further east, over the Fergana valley and the western Tarim basin, lands that were then mostly held by other Chinggisid rulers.

Its founder, Muhammad Shaybani, led the Uzbek nomads south from the steppe and took Samarkand and Bukhara from the Timurids around 1500. He drove Babur out of Central Asia, which sent Babur on to India. Shaybani was killed fighting the Safavids in 1510, but his family, the Shaybanids, held on.

Under Abdullah Khan II, in the late 16th century, Bukhara was a great centre of trade, Sunni learning and building. In 1599 the Shaybanids gave way to the Janid, or Ashtarkhanid, dynasty. In 1785 the Manghit dynasty took over and called the state the Emirate of Bukhara, which lasted until 1920.
